shower.thought: We spend our whole lives trying to find ourselves, but we're literally the one thing we can never see clearly without a mirror.
The people who say "I don't care what anyone thinks" usually care very much—they've just picked a different group to care about.
You've probably had the same conversation with different people and gotten completely different versions of who you are.
Silence is the only thing that gets louder the older you get.
Most of us are just trying to be the version of ourselves that would impress our younger self, not realizing our younger self would probably be disappointed we're still thinking about their opinion.
The scariest thing about time isn't that it runs out—it's that you don't notice it running out until it already has.
We call it "overthinking" but maybe it's just thinking applied to something that doesn't deserve that much attention.
You can't actually prove you understand something; you can only prove you can explain it to someone else.
The reason we hate waiting is because it's the only time we can't distract ourselves from the fact that we're just... here.
Forgetting someone's name after they tell you is somehow more insulting than if you'd never learned it at all.
Your taste in music is basically a time capsule of whoever you were when you stopped listening to new artists.
The worst part of knowing too much is realizing how much confidently wrong everyone around you is.
We treat our phones like they're part of our bodies, which is funny because we're slowly losing the ability to do the things our bodies could do before we had them.
Sarcasm is just honesty with a safety net.
You never truly know if you're lazy or just not interested in the thing you're supposed to be doing.
The people closest to you know your worst moments but choose to stay anyway, which is probably the realest form of love that exists.
Your biggest insecurity is probably something nobody else has ever noticed about you.
We're all just making it up as we go and then judging other people for making it up differently.
The more you learn about how things actually work, the less you can enjoy them the same way.
You can't control what makes you angry, only what you do after you're angry—but we blame people for the anger itself.

darkjoke.thought:
I'd make a joke about my childhood, but my therapist says we shouldn't dredge up the past.
Apparently, we should let sleeping dogs lie. Unlike my parents did.

My boss asked why I was on LinkedIn during work hours.
I said I was looking for a new job. He said that's fine, just do it on your own time.
I said I would, but I don't have any of that left.

I'm reading a book on the history of glue. I can't put it down.
My psychiatrist says that's not why I'm here.

People keep asking how I stay so positive despite my circumstances.
Easy. I've accepted that things will never get better, so everything's a pleasant surprise now.

My girlfriend said she needed space.
So I moved to a different country. She seemed upset, which I didn't expect—I thought she'd be relieved.

I told my accountant I had some offshore accounts.
Turns out he meant investments, not my attempts to swim to Canada.

My kid asked me what happens when you die.
I said, "Well, you eventually figure out if your parents were right about everything."
He said that sounded worse than the dying part.

I've started going to the gym to improve my mental health.
Turns out misery loves company, and everyone at 5 AM is equally angry at existence.

My doctor said I need to cut back on drinking.
I'm considering switching hands to even things out.

I asked my friend if he believed in an afterlife.
He said he didn't know, but his mortgage payments suggest God has a sense of humor.

My therapist says I have commitment issues.
I said I'd work on it, then never called back.

I told my landlord the apartment was too small.
He said, "Then move out."
I said, "I tried. The door frame's too narrow."

People say money can't buy happiness.
Clearly, they've never paid off a credit card.

My mom asked why I'm not married yet.
I said I'm waiting for someone who loves me as much as my student loans do.

I started meditating to deal with stress.
Now I'm just stressed in silence, which is somehow worse.

My neighbor keeps complaining about noise from my apartment.
I told him to call the cops. He said, "Why?"
I said, "Because then at least someone would come when I scream."

I've been told I'm a pessimist.
I prefer the term "realist who's right all the time."

My doctor asked if I exercise regularly.
I said, "Does running from my problems count?"
He said, "Only if you actually get away."

I asked the barber if he could make me look younger.
He said, "Sure, I'll just cut your life short."

My wife asked if I still love her after all these years.
I said, "Of course—I'm still legally obligated."
